liquidity_score_change.ladder_as_read: ⚠️ QUOTE THE ALL-IN FIELD, NOT THE HEADLINE ONE — and the feed says so itself. slippage_bps reads 0.0 at ALL FOUR rungs, which is not a free exit: the field's own slippage_bps_basis states it is 'PRICE IMPACT against this venue's own smallest quoted rung, which EXCLUDES that rung's own spread — it is not the holder's all-in cost. The all-in figure is fill_ratio.' So a 0.0 cannot be quoted as exit cost; by construction it can never show cost at the small end. All-in from fill_ratio at 2026-09-25T13:33:00Z: $1K −11.10 bps (0.998890), $10K −1.77 bps (0.999823), $50K −2.92 bps (0.999708), $100K −4.36 bps (0.999564). ⚠️ NON-MONOTONIC — the $1K rung is the WORST of the four, so a fixed spread or fee dominates at the small end and 'single-digit bps across the ladder' is true for $10K–$100K and FALSE at $1K. ⚠️ Also a stated denominator: fair_value 1.1838605621460765 with fair_value_basis 'market', not NAV — on a NAV-accruing vault share an all-in cost struck against a market fair value is not the same quantity as one struck against NAV. Direction not established here; recorded so nobody divides through it.

liquidity_score_change.not_load_bearing_correction_of_the_corre: ✅ One sub-claim in the report that prompted this does NOT survive checking, and the distinction changes where the fault lies. It said 3.39% was 'near that day's maximum'. It was not — on 2026-09-24 syrupusdt's 24 hourly reads run min 1.34%, MEDIAN 3.38%, max 3.57%, so 3.39% was essentially that DAY'S MEDIAN and the read was representative of its day. The defect is the DAY, not the hour within it: syrupusdt's ISO-weekly medians run W35 0.32%, W36 0.26%, W37 2.30%, W38 0.29%, W39 1.32%, so a day at 3.38% sits far above its own fortnight. A point read taken at a representative hour of an unrepresentative day is still a point read — but it fails for a different reason than the one reported, and the reported reason would have sent the fix at the wrong target.
liquidity_score_change.restore_trigger_sampling_rule: ⚠️ RESPECIFIED 2026-10-01, SECOND VERSION — AND THE FIRST ONE COULD NOT FIRE. THE RULE: cushion = 100 − deployment_ratio_pct; read it over TRAILING 7-DAY WINDOWS on all available hourly reads. NO ISO weeks and NO coverage floor. ⚠️ WHY BOTH WERE REMOVED, measured rather than reasoned: PegTracker's history file is a ROLLING ~30-DAY WINDOW (674 reads spanning 29d23h at 2026-10-01), so (a) an ISO week is in-progress a seventh of the time and must be excluded, and (b) a WEEK'S COVERAGE DEGRADES AS READS AGE OUT — W36 measured n=164/98% on 2026-09-25 and n=134/80% on 2026-10-01, nothing having changed but the window. The v1 rule required four consecutive weeks at ≥90% coverage INSIDE a 4.1-week window, with the oldest aging out as fast as the newest accumulated, so the count could not climb past ~3 BY CONSTRUCTION. It was unfireable. A trailing window has neither defect.

Next re-check 2026-11-01.
